Chengtu, Sze.,
June 3, 1933.
Dear Miss Smith:
Your letter arrived by the first air mail
and brought a real thrill to its recipient.
Unfortunately,
it was delivered two hours after the plane
had departed,
else I might have returned it with the same plane.
In accordance with your wishes, I am enclosing
herewith the original envelope and trust it may
enrich your
collector's archives. I do not know if we are the most interior
air mail for Asia or not, but the inauguration of the service
is providing a real thrill to the populace and great convenience
to letter writing. The plane had real difficulty in landing
on its first trip as the populace was too enthusiastic and
almost provided a human carpet for the landing.
In spite of
care several deaths occurred due to the crowd
and trampling.
The landing field is in the city but I understand that the
pilots are
seeking a larger field which may take them out of
the city.
Last November when some of Liu Sian's military
bombing planes soared over the city was to many the first
plane they had seen.
The mail planes seem a great change
in purpose to these
folks.
War continues outside the city. You recall your
trip to Kwanhsien to visit the plain's water supply. In that
section there has and is much fighting between the 24th and 28th mus,
One faction was inside the city and the other across the river.
In order to prevent crossing the dykes have been cut thereby
allowing the water to wander where it will. Many fields are
hopelessly flooded, while others are drying for want of water.
Prices of commodities have risen greatly.
To the northwest
and to the southwest many bridges have been burned and others
destroyed.
If settlement does not come soon, foreigners may
have to summer in Chengtu.
Last summer I had a most interesting trip to
Tatsienliu and beyond. My hiking took me right to the foot of
the famous Minya Konga.
I did not see any Tibetan spoons
and upon inquiry of the foreign residents there found that
they had not actually seen such styles in use. I was hoping to
fulfill your wish for one.
The scenery all thru the trip
was wonderful.
I would recommend it to any mountain minded
folk coming this way.
Again with most pleasant memories of your
visit to us here and with best wishes to Miss Hinder and
Jourself,
Most cordially,
(Sgd) VICTORIA R. PETERSON
